items.proposed_content: When an application already averages over progressions, Bombieri–Vinogradov preserves the aggregate error control the application consumes while forgetting which progression produced each error. This makes average GRH-quality information a task-aligned substitute, and stronger averaged tools can reach regimes where the pointwise GRH estimate is not the operative bound.

items.proposed_content: Deligne's method places one variety in a parameterized family so monodromy makes its Frobenius eigenvalues visible inside a controlled collection of global L-functions. Tensor powers and invariant-theoretic pole information provide arbitrarily strong tests, and positivity turns their limiting constraints into purity.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: The approximate functional equation spends functional symmetry once to compress a central value into a smooth coefficient sum of roughly square-root conductor length. Average coefficient control yields convexity, but another use of the same functional equation only returns a comparable sum; the unresolved resource is genuine cancellation in this finite arithmetic representation.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: Triple tensors, symmetric powers, and modularity are constructions that place local representation parameters or geometric data into higher-degree automorphic L-functions with known analytic properties in the cases listed. They enlarge the available analytic objects, but this span does not itself derive bounds on the original coefficients from them.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: Burgess replaces one incomplete short character sum by shifted high even moments whose expansion contains complete finite-field sums. Weil's function-field RH controls those structured complete sums, producing cancellation in ranges where number-field GRH for the original character gives no nontrivial short-sum estimate.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: Frobenius converts point counting into a linear spectral problem: fixed-point counts become traces, and zeros of the zeta numerator become inverses of eigenvalues on the Jacobian or cohomology. This representation identifies the eigenvalues but does not force their magnitude; purity requires additional structure, represented here by positivity of the Rosati involution.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: A quantum mass limit is reduced to decay of one scalar period, then a triple-product formula rewrites that period as a central L-value divided by controlled symmetric-square normalizers. Stirling's formula identifies aspect subconvexity as sufficient; the source proves only the further-factorized CM case, not general mass equidistribution.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: Within the half-plane of absolute convergence, an L-function gives paired views of the same object: a prime-indexed Euler product preserves local factorization, while multiplication of those factors produces a Dirichlet series over ideals. This span establishes the packaging and the licensed expansion, not a theorem that later global analysis controls the coefficients.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: Arbitrarily high symmetric-power Rankin–Selberg functions magnify a single local parameter inside nonnegative prime-power coefficients. If every required global function has the expected analyticity, positivity prevents cancellation from hiding an oversized local parameter, and letting the symmetric-power degree grow forces temperedness.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: Archimedean completion augments finite Euler factors with the data needed to expose analytic continuation and contragredient functional symmetry. Rankin–Selberg convolution with the dual serves a different role: it turns complex local parameters into nonnegative global coefficients, while standard cuspidal L-functions act as building blocks rather than proving all expected functorial products.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: The explicit formula is a genuine prime–zero bridge and candidate spectral actions offer suggestive re-encodings, but a representation is not useful merely because it is spectral. The missing burden is a mechanism that forces zero location; the source says current family averages and positivity are operationally successful while proposed routes from them or a future spectrum to GRH remain speculative.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: Analytic conductor combines arithmetic conductor, spectral height, and archimedean parameters into a common scale for critical values. Functional symmetry yields the convexity baseline on that scale; subconvexity asks only for a fixed power saving, a weaker target chosen because many applications need separation from convexity rather than full Lindelöf strength.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: GRH is operationally more than a zero-location slogan: the source presents critical-line location as square-root-scale cancellation in sums of local coefficients. Its usable force is uniform across families, while density theorems preserve only averaged or partial control and numerical or function-field evidence remains epistemically distinct from proof over number fields.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: Amplification combines three roles: a comparable-conductor family supplies orthogonality, positivity prevents the target contribution from cancelling, and short coefficient weights make the chosen member abnormally large. A diagonal-sized family only recovers convexity; improvement appears only if the off-diagonal correlations created by arithmetic shortening can be controlled.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: The theta decomposition E+C separates a local-density main term from a global cusp error. Subconvexity is sufficient because its power saving makes the cusp coefficient smaller than the locally positive Eisenstein coefficient; full Lindelöf or GRH strength is unnecessary once this scale separation is achieved.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: The span uses two distinct mechanisms that must not be merged. Period or Fourier-coefficient square formulas give positivity for particular central values, while mollification gives nonvanishing proportions across families; neither follows merely from locating zeros on the critical line.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: The scaling regime controls which structure survives. Unfolded high zeros of a fixed primitive L-function exhibit largely universal unitary statistics, whereas low zeros across a family retain monodromy or random-matrix symmetry type, which informs central nonvanishing proportions and moment predictions.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: Central vanishing carries information not captured by zero location alone: BSD proposes that its order equals the dimension of the rational-point group. Functional-equation sign can force a first zero, but it does not explain higher order, so the vanishing order refines the binary question of whether the center is a zero.

parent_sources.source_title: Perspectives on the Analytic Theory of L-Functions

items.proposed_content: Petersson and Kuznetsov formulas exchange spectral family correlations for a diagonal plus Bessel-weighted Kloosterman sums. The conversion is useful in both directions: finite-field square-root bounds can control automorphic averages and density questions, while spectral information can reveal cancellation among geometric sums beyond individual bounds.

items.proposed_content: The proposed bidirectional trace-formula claim is already contained in u17: Petersson and Kuznetsov convert spectral family correlations into a diagonal plus Kloosterman sums, use finite-field bounds in the spectral direction, and can be run backward to detect cancellation among Kloosterman sums. The additional parents do not create a distinct cross-unit relation as stated.

items.proposed_content: The source repeatedly replaces an inaccessible assertion about one object with observables available only after enlarging it to a family: character and progression averages preserve aggregate error control, symmetric powers magnify a local parameter inside nonnegative coefficients, and amplified family moments make a selected member dominate. Orthogonality, extra functional equations, tensor powers, and positivity are therefore distinct family-supplied resources, not interchangeable slogans.

items.proposed_content: A Frobenius spectrum identifies function-field zeta zeros but does not by itself constrain their magnitudes. Embedding a variety in a monodromy family makes those eigenvalues testable through global L-functions and all tensor powers; invariant-theoretic pole information and positivity then force purity. Family zero statistics reveal the associated symmetry, while the number-field explicit formula and proposed spectra still lack an analogous location-forcing mechanism.

items.proposed_content: Analytic conductor puts convexity and subconvexity on a common scale, and the approximate functional equation compresses a central value to a finite coefficient sum where genuine cancellation is the remaining resource. In the theta-series and triple-product applications, a fixed power saving is sufficient precisely because it makes a cusp contribution smaller than a positive local-density main term or makes a tested mass period decay; full Lindelof or GRH strength is unnecessary once that application-specific separation is achieved.
